full_judgment:
8. Mr Md Abdul Alim Miah Juwel, the learned Advocate appearing for the accused-appellant identified the accused-appellant before this court and submits that the accused-appellant and the complainant-respondent are Ml brother and they have entered into a compromise with the help of their relatives and friends and compromised the matter on the terms and conditions which stated in the application for compromise. He summits that the complainant-respondent will get 50% of the cheque amount which was deposited by the accused-appellant at the time of filing appeal. He lastly submits that since both the parties have entered into compromise and settled the dispute between them and he prayed for allowed the appeal and acquittal the accused-appellant from the charge on the basis of compromise. 

 9. Mr Md Shahjahan, the learned Advocate appearing for the complainant-respondent identified the complainant-respondent and conceded the submissions of the learned Advocate for the accused-appellant and submits that he has instruction from his client that they have entered into compromise and accordingly they have submitted an application for compromise before this Court and he has no objection if the accused-appellant is acquitted from the charge on the basis of compromise. 

 10. Mr Md Zakir Hossain, the learned Assistant Attorney-General identified the accused-appellant and the complainant-respondent comparing with their NID card and submits that since both the parties have entered into compromise and settled the dispute the State has nothing to oppose. On perusal of the record it appears that the accused-appellant issued a cheque of Taka 30,50,000 (thirty lac fifty thousand) in favour of the complainant-respondent to purchase 3¾ katha of land and accordingly the complainant entered into an agreement of sale with Kazi Faizul Kabir, power of attorney holder of Kati Shamsunnahar. The complainant-respondent paid Taka 30,50,000 (thirty lac fifty thotisand) only as consideration money. The accused-appellant expressed his interest to purchase the schedule land and accordingly he issued a cheque of Taka 30,50,000 (thirty lac fifty thousand) in favour of the complainant in presence of witnesses. The complamant-respondent deposited the cheque for encashment which was dishonoured for insufficient of fund. The complainant-respondent issued legal notice through his engaged lawyer informing him that cheque has been dishonoured which was issued by him but the accused-appellant did not arrange to pay the cheque money. 

 12. However, it appears that the complainant-respondent and the accused-appellant have entered into compromise and settled the dispute between them on payment of Taka 1 5,25,000 (fifteen lac twenty five thousand) only in cash and rest Taka 15,25000 (fifteen lac twenty five thousand) deposited at the time of filing appeal. The parties are interested to compromise the dispute by some terms and conditions and accordingly, they have settled the matter out of Court and this compromise should be treated as a very special circumstances of the case. The parties have entered into compromise with following terms and conditions: 

 14. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, relevant provision of law, I'm of the view that after making full payment of cheque amount the compromise was made between the parties by executing an agreement and the compromise petition filed by the parties in the appeal be accepted. It may be mentioned here that the law encourages the compromise between the parties regarding the commission of any offence with the permission of the Court since the case is pending before this Court. I've no hesitation to allow the compromise petition and as a result, this compromise shall have the effect of acquittal of the accused-appellant. 

 15. The criminal administration of justice encourages compromise of certain disputes and some of the cases can be compounded as provided under section 345 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 16. In view of the reasons given in the compromise petition of the parties that they, in the interest of both, compromised the matter. I am of the view that permission may be given for compounding the offences and acquit the accused-appellant under section 345 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. In the circumstances, I need not decide the appeal on merit but on the ground of compromise. 

 17. However, on perusal of the record it appears that the impugned cheque of Taka 30,50,000 (thirty lac fifty thousand) out of which the accused-appellant deposited 50% of the cheque amount at the time of filing appeal and paid rest of the 50% in cash to the complainant-respondent and settled the dispute between them on compromise. I am of the view that justice will be met if the accused-appellant is not required to serve the sentence of imprisonment for a period of 1(one) year since the accused-appellant and the complainant-respondent have entered into compromise and settled the dispute on payment of the cheque amount. 

 20. Accordingly, the application for compromise is disposed of.
